extracted.subtask_description: A multi-item newspaper report summarizing diplomatic/UN proceedings, government statements, and a federal criminal sentencing; aimed at informing a general audience about international and domestic political developments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security Council election vote requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: IF ALL 59 NATIONS VOTE, EACH SUCCESSFUL CONTESTANT HAS TO GET 40 VOTES » OR A TWO-THIRDS MAJORITY.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the numerical threshold needed for election to the U.N. Security Council when all member states participate — i.e., 40 votes (two-thirds) out of 59.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-campaigning from the floor before voting
rubrics_metrics.description: Romulo made his ruling that Vishinsky was out of order; non-campaigning for candidates is permitted from the floor before the voting. (context shows speakers who attempt to campaign or take the floor to influence voting can be ruled out of order.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a procedural rule in assembly sessions, delegates must not use the floor to campaign for candidates while balloting is underway; chairs may rule such remarks out of order and cut off interpretation/translation if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: U.N. Charter principle of geographic representation for Council seats
rubrics_metrics.description: Pleadings that the Assembly should take into account Article ... of the U.N. Charter which provides the principle of geographic representation on the Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invokes Charter-based expectation that council membership should reflect geographic distribution among member states; used as a standard argument in contesting candidacies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Big Five veto authority and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: ONLY THE BIG FIVE CAN HALT ACTION ON ANY PROJECT BEFORE IT BY PLAIN VETO... A VETO CAN HALT ANY ACTION, INCLUDING REGULATION OF ARMAMENTS... AND ADMISSION OF NEW MEMBERS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes the scope of the five permanent Security Council members' veto power — they alone can block Council action on substantive matters, including sanctions, military action, arms regulation, and membership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press correspondents' conduct rules to prevent leaks
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaints that a Reuters correspondent left a news conference before it ended and that short-range radio set outside the room led to disclosures; the Association will draw up a set of principles to regulate correspondents and the room where Vishinsky spoke.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalistic/professional-standard guidance: correspondents should not leave press conferences early or create conditions (e.g., outside radio monitoring) that leak proceedings; a press association committee was appointed to draft formal rules to prevent such breaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic interpretation shutdown when speaker ruled out of order
rubrics_metrics.description: Romulo instructed the translating staff to shut off the automatic interpretation system whenever any speaker in the Assembly is ruled out of order. This would prevent translations of a delegate's remarks if they are ruled out of order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural enforcement mechanism: chair may direct interpreters to stop translation to limit dissemination of remarks the chair has declared out of order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smith Act criminal standard (conspiracy to advocate overthrow)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Smith Act it is a crime to conspire to advocate revolution; the defendants were convicted of conspiring to advocate the violent overthrow of the United States Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal standard used to prosecute political advocacy as criminal conspiracy; the news summarizes its application in a lengthy federal trial and conviction of party leaders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revised sentencing limits under 1948 Smith Act amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: A change in the Smith Act made five years the limit; Judge Medina noted that if not for this change he would have thought in terms of more than five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies statutory maximum punishment after amendment — sentencing imposed must respect the revised legislative caps (here, five years).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to appeal and potential appellate path
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices of appeal from conviction and sentence were filed; the post-trial legal battle may finally end before the United States Supreme Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporter notes procedural rights: convicted defendants may file appeals (to Circuit Courts and potentially the Supreme Court), and bail pending appeal is a discretionary judicial consideration discussed in court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contempt sanctions during trial (attorneys and others)
rubrics_metrics.description: Five defense attorneys were under jail sentences for criminal contempt during the trial; motions for reversal and new trial were denied and contempt penalties were imposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courtroom conduct rule: judges may impose contempt sanctions, including jail, on counsel or participants for violations during trial; such sanctions coexist with other trial protections but can affect counsel availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Assembly seating and chairmanship rotation practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Alphabetical seating arrangement and the chairmanship rotates; in alphabetical seating the Yugoslav delegate will sit between the United States and China, and 'the chairmanship rotates.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes customary Assembly practices for ordering seats and rotating the presiding office, which shape procedural dynamics and the optics of sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy approach to Freedom of Information covenant adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: Some delegates (e.g., DediJer/Mrs. Roosevelt) insisted that a draft convention on freedom of information should be adopted at this session even if a perfect text could not be completed; others advocated postponement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflects two procedural/policy standards: (a) adopt an imperfect but timely instrument now to establish principles, or (b) postpone drafting for fuller international agreement; both are presented as legitimate procedural options.
